brief:
Purpose and bounded deliverable:
Describe the intended user-facing result, exact identity/family and what is in/out of scope. State the required editable sources, complete transfer/runtime dependencies, previews, provenance/license, validation and handoff evidence.

Original source pin and evidence:
Give exact source asset/reference paths, family/variant, revision or SS14/source repository commit where applicable, and the native states/frames/timings relevant to the request. Say unverified if a pin/source cannot be established; do not fabricate ancestry or approval.

Identity invariants to preserve:
List silhouette, proportions, distinctive anatomy (including eye count/shape), palette/material, markings/motifs and practical gameplay-scale read. Explain what must remain distinct from neighboring family members.

Early design gate (before batch production):
Provide a small original-first source/candidate contact sheet or prototype in comparable directions, camera, scale and practical distance. State the questions and assumptions requiring owner/reviewer disposition before the full batch.

States and movement evidence:
Name required idle/walk/turn/signature-action and other in-scope states. Separate source-authentic frames/timings from labeled 3D ports/inferences and optical texture loops from mechanical clips/gameplay. Do not invent abilities, physics, AI, collision or source facts.

Departures, assumptions, exclusions:
Record hidden-depth/projection/scale/camera approximations, unsupported source evidence, exclusions, integration boundary, attribution/license constraints and package preservation requirements.

Acceptance boundary:
Specify what delivery, independent visual review, automated validation, owner acceptance and runtime/client checks each mean; do not treat one as another.
